Let the coordinate update for coordinate \(i\) be \(U_i\), so one epoch with order \(\pi\) has matrix
\[
T_\pi=U_{\pi_3}U_{\pi_2}U_{\pi_1}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{f(x_3)}{f(x_0)}
=\frac{x_0^T T_\pi^THT_\pi x_0}{x_0^T Hx_0}.
\]

By symmetry under swapping coordinates \(1\leftrightarrow 3\), we may average any distribution with its reflected distribution without increasing the worst-case ratio. Thus it suffices to use three total probabilities:
\[
a=\nu(123)+\nu(321),\quad
b=\nu(132)+\nu(312),\quad
c=\nu(213)+\nu(231),
\]
with \(a+b+c=1\).

For \(x=(s,u,s)\), the even subspace gives
\[
x^THx=4s^2+4su+2u^2,
\]
and the expected post-epoch quadratic form is
\[
\left(c+\frac{3a}{8}\right)s^2+\frac a8 su+\left(\frac b2+\frac{11a}{32}\right)u^2.
\]
The odd subspace \(x=(s,0,-s)\) gives ratio \(3a/32\), which is never the active constraint at the optimum.

Writing the even numerator as \(y^TNy\), \(y=(s,u)\), with
\[
N=
\begin{pmatrix}
c+\frac{3a}{8} & \frac a{16}\\
\frac a{16} & \frac b2+\frac{11a}{32}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
4&2\\
2&2
\end{pmatrix},
\]
the worst even ratio is the largest generalized eigenvalue of \((N,G)\). For fixed \(a\), minimizing this over \(b,c\) gives \(b=0,\ c=1-a\) in the relevant range. Then the largest eigenvalue is
\[
\lambda(a)=\frac{16-a+\sqrt{225a^2-384a+256}}{64}.
\]
Differentiating,
\[
\lambda'(a)=0
\iff
450a-384=2\sqrt{225a^2-384a+256},
\]
so
\[
a=\frac{448+6\sqrt{14}}{525}.
\]
Substitution gives
\[
\lambda_{\min}
=\frac{497+84\sqrt{14}}{2100}.
\]

This is attained by, for example,
\[
\nu(123)=\nu(321)=\frac{448+6\sqrt{14}}{1050},
\]
\[
\nu(213)=\nu(231)=\frac{77-6\sqrt{14}}{1050},
\]
and
\[
\nu(132)=\nu(312)=0.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\inf_\nu \rho(\nu)=\frac{497+84\sqrt{14}}{2100}}.
\]
